haiku-low.q1: After step 5 passes and before any new instance starts, one migration job applies pending migrations. The live release must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the column or table has been retired.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 idle instances must pass /healthz 3 times in a row, and smoke tests must pass, within 10 minutes of the first launch. Otherwise the abort path runs; the live colour is unchanged.
haiku-low.q4: One ModifyListener call points the public listener's default action at the idle target group, then reads it back. Traffic moves in one switch, not gradually.
haiku-low.q5: A 5xx rate above 1% over a trailing 5-minute window during the 15-minute watch. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and marks rolled_back. It releases the lock and terminates the new colour. Migrations are left alone.
haiku-low.q6: Until T+30, the old colour is retained and manual rollback is available. After shutdown, a problem is handled by a normal full deploy of the previous release's digest.
haiku-low.q7: Transactional migrations roll back by themselves. A failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY can leave an INVALID index, dropped by the next run. Status failed_migration, no instances launched, listener untouched, lock released, engineer reviews.
haiku-low.q8: The public listener's default action is the source of truth: its target group is live, the other is idle. The deploy checks it against the DynamoDB live item, which mirrors the listener.
haiku-low.q9: A DynamoDB lock item, written by conditional write; later merges wait in queue. It never expires on its own and is held until completion, or released on abort or rollback.
haiku-low.q10: A private test listener on port 8443, reachable only from CI runners, forwards only to the idle target group. The public listener keeps serving the old colour.
haiku-low.q11: One migration job, using the migration role, runs them. It takes the advisory lock and applies pending migrations in order, recording each in schema_migrations, so applied ones are skipped.
haiku-low.q12: After abort or rollback, their logs are saved, then the instances are deregistered and terminated. Migrations stay applied. The next deploy launches 4 fresh instances into idle.

sonnet.q1: Before any new instance starts (step 6, after lint, lock and live-state read). The release currently serving traffic (the live/old release) must keep working on the migrated schema, so migrations must be additive only.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the column or table has been retired.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must pass the health gate (streak of at least 3 each, same poll) and the smoke tests, both within 10 minutes of the first instance launching, and pass the pre-switch check. If not, the abort path runs: the listener stays on the live colour, logs are saved, new instances are terminated, status is aborted and the lock is released.
sonnet.q4: One ModifyListener call sets the public listener's default action to the idle (new) target group. It is then read back, and the state table's live item is updated.
sonnet.q5: Any 5xx-rate window above 1% during the 15-minute watch (also the fallback if the state machine cannot start). Rollback points the listener back at the old target group, sets live to the old colour, status rolled_back, releases the lock, and captures logs then terminates the new colour's instances. It leaves migrations untouched (never reversed).
sonnet.q6: Until T+30. Automatic rollback applies only during the watch (T to T+15). From T+15 to T+30 an engineer can run the manual rollback job. After T+30 the old colour is shut down, so recovery is a normal full deploy of the previous release's digest.
sonnet.q7: Status failed_migration. A transactional failure rolls back by itself. A failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY can leave an INVALID index, which the next run drops before retrying, and an engineer must review it first. No instance is launched, the listener is untouched (live colour keeps serving), and the lock is released.
sonnet.q8: Step 5 reads the public listener's default action: its target group is the live colour and the other is idle, which gets the new release. The listener is the source of truth. The state table's live item (in DynamoDB) mirrors it and must agree, otherwise the deploy aborts with live_state_unclear. Recorded in deploy#<id> as colour_new and colour_old.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a DynamoDB record acquired with a conditional write in step 4. It is held until the deploy completes (step 19, after the old colour shuts down at T+30), or released on abort or rollback. It never expires on its own, and a stale one is cleared only by an engineer. Merges that arrive meanwhile wait, and only the newest is deployed afterwards.
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener on port 8443, a private listener reachable only from CI runners that forwards only to the idle target group. Smoke tests never use the public listener.
sonnet.q11: One migration job using the migration role. It takes the PostgreSQL advisory lock so two runs cannot overlap, applies pending migrations in order, and records each in schema_migrations. The ledger means already-applied migrations are skipped, and the deploy lock allows only one deploy at a time.
sonnet.q12: They are terminated (after capturing logs). On abort they are deregistered and terminated, and on rollback logs are captured and then they are terminated. The idle colour is not running between deploys, since each deploy launches 4 new instances. Migrations stay applied, so the next deploy skips them because they are in the ledger. The fix is a forward release.
